reviews.review:
"玄龙棋MysteryChess" is a somewhat needlessly convoluted "chess-like" turn based strategy game where you move various pieces that have attack/defense values.  You can take other pieces if your attack beats their defense.  The pieces have various movement capabilities (but not analogs of Chess or Chinese Chess, so calling this game Chess is highly misleading).  The UI does have an English translation to some extent but gameplay is still mostly bewildering to the point of being nonsensical, and certainly not worth the effort of bothering to learn given how lazy the technical implementation is.

There's no options to change the resolution for the game or customise the graphics settings.  There's no way for gamers to ensure this is running at the native resolution of their displays... there's no guarantee this game will look right on any PC as a result of this hamfisted design decision.  There's no way for gamers to try improve the low quality graphics.  The implementation here is of such poor quality, the developer couldn't work out how to make the game display in fullscreen, it only runs in a window.  The controls can't be customised, which will be an annoyance for many, but it can also render the game unplayable for differently-abled gamers.

Problematically, the user interface for this game is just a 2D text heavy panel with a few static images... it might as well be a browser game.  And we all know, Steam isn't here to compete with Chrome and Firefox.  If the game can be done in a web browser, it's just not rich or compelling enough to appeal to serious gamers.  Even worse, the game was written in Java (I'm not making this up).  Talk about not using the right tools for the job.  Might as well try to bake a cake with a screwdriver.  The extremely poor choice of game engine here is a major contributing factor to the defects with the game.

These technical defects push this game below acceptable standards for any modern PC game.
